title: Saint Benedict receiving Maurus and Placidus
medium: Black and red chalk, pen and brown ink, brown and grey wash, squared in black chalk, partially indented with stylus, an added section of paper at the left of the sheet

events.q: A remarkable early drawing by Raphael, this sheet can be dated to circa 1503

events.n: a collection formed in Tuscany in the 18th century
events.q: From a collection formed in Tuscany in the 18th century.

events.n: Anonymous sale; lot 27, as 'Attributed to Raphael'
events.q: Anonymous sale; Christie's, London, 19 April 1988, lot 27, as 'Attributed to Raphael'.
on loan to the Fogg Art Museum, Harvard University, Cambridge, Massachusetts.
John Shearman is recorded as having endorsed the attribution on 11 January 1989

events.n: letter to the present owner confirming the attribution
events.q: Paul Joannides also confirmed his belief in the attribution in a letter to the present owner dated 24 August 1990
As Laurence Kanter was the first to recognize (Andersen, _op. cit_., p. 50), Raphael's drawing represents one of the key episodes in the history of the Benedictine Order

events.n: letter to the present owner accepting the attribution
events.q: Konrad Oberhuber wrote to the present owner on 10 September 1990 that he was convinced it was from the hand of Raphael
